section_summary: This section finishes a biographical “Who’s Who” of Japanese newspaper, news-agency and broadcasting personnel, recording their careers, affiliations, publications and addresses. It then begins a statistical newspaper directory covering Tokyo, Osaka, Kanto, Tohoku, Chubu, Hokuriku and Kinki, followed by the opening of the Chugoku district, with circulation, advertising rates, officers, news-service affiliations, equipment, publications and staffing. Together the documents provide a detailed snapshot of Japan’s postwar press organization and leadership.

subfiles.title: Who’s Who: Japanese Press Personnel
subfiles.about: Biographical entries identify leading Japanese newspaper, news-agency and broadcasting personnel and summarize their careers, posts, publications and addresses.
subfiles.summary: This portion continues alphabetically from Maeda and Matsui through Zentoku. It covers editors, publishers, business managers, correspondents, broadcasting officials and press scholars associated with national and regional Japanese media. Several entries identify people removed under the postwar purge, while others document wartime assignments in China, Southeast Asia, Europe and the United States. The final page completes the biographical sequence immediately before the statistical newspaper directory begins.

subfiles.title: Newspaper Directory: Tokyo through Kinki Districts and opening of Chugoku District
subfiles.about: Tables profile Japanese newspapers by district, giving circulation, address, advertising rates, corporate officers, editorial staff, agency affiliations, equipment, publications and employee totals.
subfiles.summary: The directory begins with Tokyo newspapers and news services, continues through Osaka, and then organizes the provincial press into Kanto, Tohoku, Chubu, Hokuriku and Kinki districts. Alternating pages supply corporate and editorial data and then technical information on branch offices, news agencies, supplementary publications, presses and departmental staffing. National titles such as Asahi, Mainichi, Yomiuri and Nihon Keizai appear alongside a wide range of regional and evening papers. Page 171 opens the Chugoku district with entries for papers in Yamaguchi, Hiroshima, Okayama, Tottori and Shimane, and the directory clearly continues beyond this section.
